After missing last season with a torn Achilles, he will make $13.4 M this season with a $14.1 M player option for 2027-28. 2). When he signed with Portland - where he's obviously an icon - last summer, he said "definitely my plan is to be playing for the Trail Blazers in my last game of my career." title: There’s no good option really. Social support and doing what you are good at is part of the best treatment for Sorsby’s issues and that ended at TTU. NFL has declared war on him by manufacturing a process issue for his straightfoward application for the supplemental draft. The best approach would be the lawyers figuring out a way forward that would be sufficient to satisfy the NFL and provide certainty and peace for the player and teams. But that makes way too much sense when Sorsby is just a labor law pawn, content to some, and not a human being. And that approach is way too kind and human given the FTG Doctrine that controls most high profile things in the internet era. Just billables and interesting legal issues and not human. So the way they will likely deal with the dude going thru addiction treatment and anxiety is maximizing the uncertainty of whether he will ever have the opportunity to do the thing he loved so that the billable hours can be huge and wasteful. Being truthful about addiction and bad mistakes is often punished extremely harshly. It’s what makes it easier to extort people. And make it harder to get help. Every day, I am reminded of how grateful I am that I wasn’t raised during the skynet addiction machine era. I hope the best for Sorsby and his family, and I hope all the grown ass adults don’t keep making it worse.

title: Yesterday was a really fun day to be covering DC sports and to be a part of the @1067theFan team. We had Nats star James Wood in studio for an interview and some fun social content. If you haven't seen his hilarious "This is SportsCenter" style commercial check my IG account. It's great. https://t.co/t3JSjDJl92. We also did a live show from the Anthem ahead of the NBA Draft. It was the kind of day @FunnyDanny (a diehard Wiz fan forever) and I have been dreaming of for a long time. People were Wizards-crazed all day. Then I hung out with @JunksRadio and chipped in on our Junkies draft show. That was a treat and something the 10-year-old version of me wouldn't have believed I was getting to do. Always very cool to get to be on air with @EBJunkies @Moneymetal and @GlassJoeJP after growing up listening to them for so many years. But it's especially neat to be able to join them on a night when we are talking with guests like Wizards POBO Michael Winger, @davidaldridgedc and @JohnWall on site. What a life we are living. Meanwhile the Caps were pulling off a block buster trade and the Nats were going toe to toe with the Phillies at Nats Park. Just a crazy day in DC sports. Huge props to @Tobi_Altizer and @strobersports for a lot of hard work behind the scenes (in addition to crushing it on a late-night show from the draft party). Also to producer @DADameron for a lot of coordination and hectic work back in studio while not getting to be part of the action in the field, which isn't always fun I'm sure. Additionally, I've got to give props to @MetalChris for a long, hard day that went very smoothly and the contributions @kdido5 made to the show and our coverage. It was a fun night kicking it with @drabtshirt and @Nell_BTP and our crew during the draft. I've stolen Ernie Johnson's saying and use it all the time as my own now. My job is a "get to" job not a "have to" job. Yesterday was a "get to" day and it was cool to be a part of.
